title: Substitute
text: Let $$x=tan(\theta)$$. Then the integral becomes the integral of $$cos^2\left(\theta\right)$$ with respect to θ.

title: Integrate and convert back
text: The integral is $$\frac{\theta}{2}+\frac{1}{2} sin\left(\theta\right) cos\left(\theta\right)$$. Here θ is arctan(x), and $$sin\left(\theta\right) cos\left(\theta\right)=\frac{x}{1+x^2}$$.
